summary: Do not ship this design yet. Round-one F1-F3 are substantively addressed: AC5 covers inherited WIENERDOG_JOB without a valid token, catch-up uses the token-minting runJob path, Windows is explicitly left unchanged, only step 19 filters, AC6a-d assert digest content, and the config-removal mutation targets AC4. However, the claimed B1/B2-only residual is incomplete and not temporally bounded, and recovery-render failure can silently leave the digest filtered.

findings.title: The B1/B2-only narrowing omits ordinary job failures and has no finite bound
findings.body: A normal dream-body failure is recorded by run-job only after the child exits: run-job.js:1226-1269 writes last_status:error and calls failLoud, which appends the new job-failure alert at :1257. If the preceding successful run filtered the old dream callout, and the next run fails before step 19 without a quarantine refresh, digest.md remains clean while alerts.jsonl contains a genuine unresolved failure. Even when l.724 ran, it ran before this new alert existed. AC6a/AC6b can prove that a pre-existing record remains visible, but they do not prove visibility of the fresh parent-appended failure. This is another out-of-process false negative beyond B1/B2. The advertised recovery bound is also not finite: l.724 is conditional on newlyQuarantined, sync is attended-only, and every subsequent successful step-19 render filters the job again. A genuine failure can therefore remain absent for its entire unresolved lifetime.
findings.recommendation: Expand the residual to every run-job failLoud append made after the child exits, remove the claim that B1/B2 are the sole narrowing, and add an end-to-end criterion starting from a clean digest that makes the dream child fail and asserts both the newly appended alert and final digest content. Either provide a deterministic supervisor-side notification surface or obtain explicit owner acceptance of potentially indefinite digest omission.

findings.title: A failed recovery render is swallowed and leaves no diagnostic for the still-filtered digest
findings.body: regenerateDigest performs several fallible reads and an atomic write. The design requires its recovery failure to be swallowed so the original post-step-19 error wins, but requires no secondary stderr report and AC7 does not cover a recovery-render exception. If that render fails, the atomic writer preserves the previous filtered digest; run-job subsequently appends the genuine failure, and users receive neither its callout nor any indication that restoration failed. This contradicts the stated principle that a failure after the filtered render restores every omitted callout.
findings.recommendation: Keep the original exception as the propagated error, but report the recovery-render exception separately on stderr, name the resulting inability to restore as a residual, and add an AC7 case that injects recovery-render failure and verifies the original error, the secondary diagnostic, and the unchanged filtered digest.
